title: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
claim: Distilling raw experience, including failures, into reusable structured knowledge lets agents improve faster and reach higher performance than raw-memory baselines.
layout: 2 stacked panels: (a) left-to-right pipeline on top, (b) training curves below
description: The figure has two stacked panels. Panel (a) is a left-to-right icon pipeline. A base-model robot and an environment laptop are linked by a cycle arrow. They feed a trajectory icon, which splits into a green check (success) and a red cross (failure). Gray dashed arrows show the prior path: successes go to Memory (a stack of books) and failures go to a trash can labeled Discard. Colored solid arrows show the new path: both outcomes go through an Expert scroll icon, then to Memory, then to a Skills folder. A red evolve loop turns the base robot into an upgraded robot. Panel (b) is a line plot of success rate against training steps. A red SkillRL curve rises fastest and plateaus around 90%. Blue vanilla GRPO and gray dashed GRPO+Memory curves stay lower. Dashed guide lines and star, square and triangle markers show convergence points. A callout reads 'Higher Performance, Faster Convergence'.
caption: (a) Overview of the SKILLRL pipeline. Unlike previous methods (gray dashed lines) that store raw trajectories and discard failures, SKILLRL employs an experiencebased distillation mechanism to transform diverse experiences into structured skills. (b) Performance on ALFWorld validation set. SKILLRL achieves faster convergence and superior success rates compared to vanilla GRPO and memoryaugmented RL.
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have shown stunning results in complex tasks, yet they often operate in isolation, failing to learn from past experiences. Existing memory-based methods primarily store raw trajectories, which are often redundant and noise-heavy. This prevents agents from extracting high-level, reusable behavioral patterns that are essential for generalization. In this paper, we propose SkillRL, a framework that bridges the gap between raw experience and policy improvement through automatic skill discovery and recursive evolution. Our approach introduces an experience-based distillation mechanism to build a hierarchical skill library SkillBank, an adaptive retrieval strategy for general and task-specific heuristics, and a recursive evolution mechanism that allows the skill library to co-evolve with the agent's policy during reinforcement learning. These innovations significantly reduce the token footprint while enhancing reasoning utility. Experimental results on ALFWorld, WebShop and seven search-augmented tasks demonstrate that SkillRL achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming strong baselines over 15.3% and maintaining robustness as task complexity increases. Code is available at this https://github.com/aiming-lab/SkillRL.
